problem: The latch-up parasitic bipolar path is pointed to two different chapters. Section 1 says the parasitic devices are covered in Chapter 2.8, but Section 3 says 'The bipolar path itself is left to Chapter 2.5.' The parasitic npn/pnp path is exactly the latch-up mechanism of Chapter 2.8, so the student is sent to the wrong chapter.
fix: Change to: 'The parasitic bipolar path itself is left to Chapter 2.8.' or delete the sentence, keeping only one cross-reference for latch-up.

problem: 'the substrate tie to VSS is thick and low resistance' mixes up the tie contact with the substrate. A tie is a small p+ contact; it is the substrate that is thick and gives a low resistance path.
fix: Write: 'the p-substrate is thick, so the path from the substrate to the VSS pad has low resistance, which shunts the parasitic path that causes latch-up'.

problem: The table gives only 'p-substrate to VSS' for twin-tub. With a p-type starting wafer the p-well is part of the same p region and is also tied to VSS; without saying so, a student may think the p-well body is left floating or needs its own pad.
fix: Add to the substrate-tie cell: 'p-well and p-substrate both to VSS (n-well to VDD)'.
